subject: Question about calculated "L" in estimation results

messages.author: 873771e17199598a
messages.subject: Question about calculated "L" in estimation results
parts:
Hello, 

I am using the Distance software to generate abundance and density estimates for large whales, post stratified by species, region, season, and year to generate abundance and density estimates for each species by region, season and year. I have the best model and currently looking through the results windows.

An issue I see is that distance has estimated my "L" (total length of transect line(s)) to be the same for each stratum, which is an issue because the total length of transect lines covered varies by season and year, i.e. there are yearly and seasonal differences in amount and length of transects covered. I'm concerned because that means my estimate for number of clusters of animals seen per transect length is off. Anyone have any insight/troubleshoot info for this? Thanks!

messages.author: f2122b34f1aa6e95
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Question about calculated "L" in estimation results
parts:
Hillary

I see the effort issue when you post-stratify using covariates in the observation layer is still bothering you.  My comments on the subject in my 19Apr19 reply may not have convinced you that Distance is performing properly.  So I'll try again.

In your next to the last sentence you suggest that the encounter rate (number of clusters per unit of effort) is "off".  I'm guessing you are specifying some or most of your stratification criteria at the observation layer.  My earlier reply showed what happens in the encounter rate calculation when post-stratifying by a field in the observation layer.

A way to check results would be to make actual strata from each possible combination of species/region/season/year (at the stratum level of your project).  Then use that field for stratification.  You would then specify effort explicitly for each of the strata.  I presume you would specify identical effort for species1 in summer/2015/area1 and for species2 in summer/2015/area1, would you not?  That is what Distance is doing in its post-stratification calculations.

Happy for you to elaborate on your comment about encounter rate being 'off'.
